# Example: one FIXML trade capture report

[`sample_trade_capture_report.xml`](sample_trade_capture_report.xml) is one
FIXML `Batch` of `TrdCaptRpt` messages, as `scripts/render_fixml.py` writes
them, trimmed to five trades so the cases are easy to see. The header, the
`Batch` wrapper and `TotMsg="5"` are as rendered.

**Every value in it is synthetic**: generated by
`scripts/generate_synthetic.py` (default seed) and built by `dbt build`. The
sender id is a placeholder. Field mapping and conventions:
[`docs/FIXML_MAPPING.md`](../FIXML_MAPPING.md).

## Which trade shows which case

All five are combos (multi-leg parlays) traded on 2025-03-10. `LastPx` is
always the YES price; for a NO trade the trade price is 1 − `LastPx`, and
`GrossTrdAmt` = `LastQty` × the trade price.

| `TrdID` (prefix) | Case | What to look at |
|---|---|---|
| `c490d894` | **YES buy** (maker) | `Side="1"`, `AgrsrInd="N"`; `MiscFees` holds the fee; `TrdRptOrdDetl` links the bot's quote (`RefOrdID`, `RefOrdIDSrc="5"`); `Txt` carries the RFQ id |
| `e45e73d7` | **NO buy** (maker) | `Side="2"`; `LastPx="0.110000"` is the YES price, so the NO price is 0.89 and `GrossTrdAmt` = 320.24 × 0.89 |
| `37ac40f3` | **Scalar-settled combo** | A leg of this combo later settled at a fractional value. A trade report records the trade, not the settlement, so the message looks like any other YES buy; the settlement is graded in `int_fills_graded` and reconciled in `recon_fills_python_vs_dbt` |
| `546fb56d` | **Unknown fee, estimated cost** (NO buy) | No `MiscFees` element (never a zero fee); `Txt="fee=unknown;cost_estimated=Y"`; no quote id, so no `RefOrdID` |
| `45da5c07` | **Taker fill** (a taker-script trade) | `AgrsrInd="Y"` (this account took the price); no quote reference, since the account was not quoting |

## How it was produced

After `python scripts/generate_synthetic.py` and `dbt build`:

```bash
python scripts/render_fixml.py --dates 2025-03-10 \
  --trade-ids c490d894-566f-4161-a232-dd956cfa30b7,e45e73d7-3c37-4041-aff2-8ee17229bc85,37ac40f3-47bb-4566-b828-e5888b14f876,546fb56d-fa8a-452c-a7ed-1a992abfc5d7,45da5c07-ac27-4cf7-9384-e7767cd26f30 \
  --created-at 2025-03-11T11:00:00Z \
  --out-file docs/examples/sample_trade_capture_report.xml
python scripts/check_fixml.py --file docs/examples/sample_trade_capture_report.xml
```

The trades are the ones the pipeline's own sampling rule picked for that
date's full sample file (`work/fixml/trade_capture_20250310.fixml.xml`).

## How it is kept honest

`scripts/run_all.py`, and so CI on every push, re-renders this file from the
fresh build and fails unless the result is byte-identical to the committed
file. It then runs `check_fixml.py --file` on it: every trade must
round-trip field by field to `mart_daily_trade_report`. Locally, the same
check also validates it against the FIX schema; CI skips that half (see
[FIXML_MAPPING.md](../FIXML_MAPPING.md#schema-and-validation)).
